items.label: section_header
items.text: HIGHPERFORMANCELIQUIDCHROMATOGRAPHY

items.label: text
items.text: High performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) is a refinement of column chromatography, described in Section 15E.1. The main differences are:

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·The solvent is forced through a metal tube under high pressure, rather than being allowed to pass through by gravity.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The particle size of the stationary phase is much smaller, which leadstobetterseparationofthecomponents.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Thesampleis injectedinto thecolumn.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The components are detected after passing through the column, usually by their absorption of ultraviolet radiation.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The wholeprocess is automated, and the results are quickly available on a computer display.

items.label: section_header
items.text: GASCHROMATOGRAPHY

items.label: text
items.text: Gas chromatography(GC) is another refinement of column chromatography.Themaindifferences are:

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·Themetaltubecanbeseveralmetreslongandiscoiledtosave space.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The stationary phase is a solid or liquid coated on the inside of the tube.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The mobile phase is an inert carrier gas (often nitrogen or helium)

items.label: list_item
items.text: The sample is injected into the column, as in HPLC.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The components passing through the column are detected.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The whole process is automated, and the results are quickly available on a computer display (fig B).
